clue.text: Neighbourhood wanting police officer to be authoritarian

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the officer's letters are taken away from the neighbourhood word

blocks.note: a district is a neighbourhood
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A local community wants its policeman to take a hard line.
explanation.walkthrough: Take DI away from the front of DISTRICT to leave STRICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict person demands obedience and enforces rules firmly, which is what an authoritarian does.

clue.text: Give in as say, snot's brought up containing cold bacteria's source

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
containing means holding inside, so the reversed word wraps around the cold letter
a source is where something starts, so take the opening letter of bacteria

blocks.note: snot is an example of mucus, hence as say
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
the first letter of bacteria

explanation.surface: A cold sufferer coughs up phlegm laden with germs and gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As say' marks snot as one example of the wider word; brought up suits a down answer, where the letters climb from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to yield or give way, especially to illness or pressure.

clue.text: Nonconformist bishop's breaking wind

indicators.note: something breaking into a word bursts in, so the bishop sits inside the other word

blocks.note: to reel in a line is to wind it
B is bishop in chess notation

explanation.surface: An unconventional clergyman scandalises everyone by passing wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as flatulence, but it is the verb that rhymes with find.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel refuses to conform to authority or convention, so is a nonconformist.

clue.text: Someone who loves Charlie Chaplin's debut – short act prepared with dedication

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so take the first letter of the comedian's name
short means cut off, so the word act loses its last letter
something prepared is made ready by working it up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of Chaplin
act with its tail cut
taken as written into the anagram

explanation.surface: A fan of Charlie Chaplin admires the way the star's early short films were made with real commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is slang for cocaine, not the silent-film comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is slang for cocaine, so someone who loves it, compulsively, is a cocaine addict.

clue.text: Journalist is getting to grips with court rulings

indicators.note: to get to grips with something is to grasp it, so these letters hold the court abbreviation

blocks.note: ED is short for editor
taken as written
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A reporter is wrestling with the judgements handed down by a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court rulings' reads as one phrase, but the definition is rulings alone and court only supplies its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Edicts are official orders or decrees issued by an authority, so they are rulings.

clue.text: Film star's fans found him wandering around middle of Luton

indicators.note: middle of asks for the central letter of the town's name
wandering around means straying aimlessly, so the letters move out of their order with the extra one mixed in

blocks.note: taken as written into the anagram
the third of five letters

explanation.surface: Admirers of a movie star spot him strolling round Luton.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is an English town north of London, an unlikely haunt for a Hollywood star; around tells you the central letter joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Dustin Hoffman is an Oscar-winning American actor, star of The Graduate and Rain Man.

clue.text: Miss film's opening to get model?

indicators.note: opening means coming first, so the film word leads and the miss word follows

blocks.note: a film is a thin covering layer
Miss is the title for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman's screen debut leads to a modelling contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: not every model is a cover girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover girl is a model whose photograph appears on the front of a magazine.

clue.text: Separate ends of ship illuminated

indicators.note: ends of asks for the first and last letters of the vessel word

blocks.note: the outer letters of ship
lit up means illuminated

explanation.surface: The bow and stern of a vessel are both floodlit at night.
explanation.definitionFit: To split up is to part company or divide, which is to separate.

clue.text: Instruction for division from yank – literally 3 over 3's helping to begin with

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means placed above, so the number word sits on top of the next piece

blocks.note: the figure 3 spelt out as a word
3 points to 3-down, cocaine, and a helping of cocaine is a line
to whip something away is to yank it

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle: an instruction to divide, with 3 written over 3.
explanation.walkthrough: A division is a vote in the UK Parliament, not arithmetic. 3 refers to the answer at 3-down; to begin with puts the first two pieces before the yank word.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-line whip is a party's strictest order to its MPs to attend and vote a certain way in a parliamentary division.

clue.text: Crust should colour artisan bread first of all

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of every word that follows the definition

blocks.note: the initials of these four words

explanation.surface: Baking advice: the crust of a craft loaf ought to be browned first.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the hard crust that forms over a healing wound.

clue.text: As one actor appears occasionally – the boy's four, see

indicators.note: something that appears only occasionally shows up every other time, so take alternate letters of the word actor

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of actor
the boy is = he's
four in Roman numerals
Ely is a bishop's see, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A child actor makes the odd appearance in a play, and here the four-year-old boy can be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's seat is called a see, and ELY is the crossword's favourite one.
explanation.definitionFit: To act cohesively is to act together in unity, as if one body.

clue.text: New clue's badly constructed using indicator, initially for 'middle parts'

indicators.note: something badly constructed is put together wrongly, so the word clue is rearranged
initially points to the opening letter of the preceding word indicator

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
the letters of clue in a new order
the opening letter of indicator

explanation.surface: A self-referential grumble about a fresh crossword clue whose indicator is clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pokes fun at cryptic-clue jargon: indicator really is just a word giving its first letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclei is the plural of nucleus, the central core of an atom or cell, so they are middle parts.

clue.text: Change state of emergency, essentially – maybe Qatar's hosting

indicators.note: essentially points to the core, the single central letter of the word emergency
a host takes a guest inside, so the Gulf state's word wraps around the central letter

blocks.note: Qatar is an example of an emirate, hence maybe
the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: A national emergency, perhaps with Qatar hosting the World Cup, prompts a change of state.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: to change the state you live in.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave your own country to settle in another, literally a change of state.

clue.text: Suffering embarrassment when skilfully taking a cast off

definitions.note: an adverb; read it as 'while suffering embarrassment'

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so the skilful word swallows the other pieces

blocks.note: ably means skilfully
taken as written
to shed is to cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: An angler or a knitter feels awkward when deftly casting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast off' looks like a knitting or sailing term, but it is a verb meaning discard, like a snake's old skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashedly describes doing something in an embarrassed, self-conscious manner.

clue.text: Partners ask Nike to change leather

indicators.note: to change the letters is to alter their order

blocks.note: North and South are partners in bridge
taken as written into the anagram

explanation.surface: Business partners ask the sportswear firm Nike to switch to a different leather.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, North and South play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakeskin is the treated skin of a snake, used as a decorative leather.

clue.text: Feeble Fed's quietly pursuing cartel at last

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the setter's piece comes after the cartel letter
at last points to the final letter of the word cartel

blocks.note: the last letter of cartel
Fed is the setter, so Fed's is I'm
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A weak Federal agent quietly tails a drug cartel.
explanation.walkthrough: Fed is this puzzle's setter, so the setter's own name becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means lacking firmness or energy, which is a synonym of feeble.

clue.text: To begin with, 'anon' means in the future

indicators.note: to begin with asks for only the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: the first letter of anon
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: A note on usage: the old word anon signifies some time later.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says anon means later, which is true, but anon only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Away can describe time still to come, as in Christmas is three weeks away.

clue.text: Pavlov commands a dog using prime bits of fatty food?

indicators.note: prime bits are the letters in prime-numbered positions: second, third, fifth, seventh and so on

blocks.note: letters 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 and 17 of the run

explanation.surface: Pavlov trains his dog with treats of rich food.
explanation.walkthrough: Count the letters of the whole run as one string; 'prime' looks like 'best', but means the primes 2, 3, 5, 7.
explanation.definitionFit: An avocado is a fruit unusually high in fat, so it is a fatty food, by example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Nurse infant over advanced influenza, finally getting spicy food

indicators.note: the child word stretches over the advanced letter, covering it on both sides
finally points to the last letter of influenza

blocks.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
an infant is a young child
A is the abbreviation for advanced
the final letter of influenza

explanation.surface: A sick child is nursed through a bad bout of flu and finally gets something spicy to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish, a tortilla rolled round a filling and covered in chilli sauce.

clue.text: See 5
Beatnik recalled poo lining old river

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards
a lining surrounds what it lines, so the dung word goes around the others

blocks.note: a turd is a piece of poo
O is the abbreviation for old
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A beat poet remembers excrement lining the banks of an ancient river.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, lining should put the poo word inside, but here it goes around the old river pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A beatnik rejected conventional society, the sort of person called a dropout.

clue.text: See 3
Produce example Nectar card – store review all terms

indicators.note: a term is an end, so every one of the next words gives its closing letter

blocks.note: honey is one example of a nectar, a sweet drink of the gods
the last letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A shopper examines a supermarket loyalty card and the terms and conditions of a store review.
explanation.walkthrough: Nectar is a UK loyalty card scheme, which the surface leans on; here Nectar is a sweet drink, and Produce is fruit and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeydew is a kind of melon, an item of fresh produce sold by greengrocers.

clue.text: Group of footballers – big characters from Tottenham Hotspur – come stripped to work out

indicators.note: big characters are capital letters, so take only the capitals of the club's name
something stripped has its outer layer removed, so the word come loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: the FA is the Football Association
the two capital letters, which open each word
the inside of the word come

explanation.surface: A footballing body and the stars of Spurs arrive in their kit, ready to train.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur, known as Spurs, is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to understand it after thought, which is to work it out.

clue.text: Why some like Mars being in transit regularly with Earth

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so take every other letter of the word transit

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: An astronomer explains why the planet Mars, regularly crossing in front of the Sun, appeals to stargazers.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars is not the planet but the Mars bar, a British chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: People like a Mars bar because of its taste, its flavour.

clue.text: Journalist is working with ITV before mass protest of a modern variety

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked over and moved into a new order

blocks.note: a hack is a journalist, usually a jobbing one
taken as written
taken as written
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A reporter goes to work at the ITV television network before covering a large modern demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV is a British commercial television channel; before puts the mass letter after the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacktivism is political protest carried out by hacking computer systems, a recent kind of activism.

clue.text: Deposit's unreasonably small on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: too means excessively, beyond reason
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Looking back, a tenant decides the deposit demanded is far too little.
explanation.definitionFit: Soot is the black powdery residue that a fire leaves deposited inside a chimney.

clue.text: Busy men with a net at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
the letters of a net rearranged

explanation.surface: Crewmen are hard at work handling a net out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Busy here means fussy or over-decorated, not occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy design is crowded with detail, which is what ornate means: elaborately decorated.

clue.text: Spoil hot iron with constant temperature

blocks.note: hot and in both mean fashionable
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
c is a constant in maths and physics
T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: Pressing clothes with a hot iron at a fixed setting can ruin them.
explanation.definitionFit: To infect is to contaminate or taint something, which is to spoil it.
